senses.gloss: f. (Ispe. noun of טל, טלל; cmp. טַלִּית) robe, garment.
units: <cite ref="Targum Jonathan on Genesis 9:23">Targ. Y. Gen. IX, 23</cite>; a. fr.—
<cite ref="Shabbat 128a:10">Sabb. 128ᵃ</cite> <he>א׳ הראוייה לו</he> a robe becoming his position.
<cite ref="Moed Katan 28b:7">M. Kat. 28ᵇ</cite> (prov.) <he>שיול א׳ וכ׳</he> the grave is a fine robe for the freeman whose outfit is complete (well becoming old and virtuous age).
B. Mets. 17ᵃ; a. e.—Pl. אִסְטְלִין, אִסְטְלֵי, אִסְטַלְוָון, אִצְ׳ &c. א׳ דלבושין a suit of clothes.

<cite ref="Onkelos Genesis 45:22">Targ. Gen. XLV, 22</cite>; (ed. Berl. <he>אוּסְטְלַוָּן</he>; <cite ref="Onkelos Genesis 45:22">ib.</cite> Y. <he>אסטלוי ולבוש</he>, read <he>אסטלי דלבוש</he>).—Y. Ber. III, 6ᵈ bot. (v. margin. note ed. Krot.).

<cite ref="Kohelet Rabbah 11:1">Koh. R. to XI, 1</cite> <he>א׳ דלבושן</he> v. supra.—Cmp. <cite ref="A02381"><he>אִסְטַלִּית</he></cite>.—[<cite ref="Jerusalem Talmud Shekalim 3:3:3">Y. Shek. III, 47ᶜ</cite> bot. <he>אסטלי של זהב</he>, read <he>אִיסְטְרֵי</he>; v. <cite ref="A01521"><he>אִיסְתִּירָא</he></cite>.] [Although our w. coincides, in meaning and sound, with στολή in its poëtic and older sense as ‘an outfit’, yet the form of its Hebrew equivalent (<cite ref="A02381"><he>אסטלית</he></cite>) and the laws regulating the borrowing of words, as well as its appearance in so remote a dialect as the Mandaic (as <he>עצטלא</he>) forbid the derivation from the Greek.]
